ITQAN:v3p103/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r10.claim: An active participle can carry passive meaning: ماء دافق is poured water, لا عاصم means none protected, and آمنا means made secure.
ITQAN:v3p103/r10.anchor: ومنها إطلاق فاعل على مفعول نحو ﴿ ماء دافق ﴾ أي مدفوق

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r1.claim: Dafq means pouring: the water is poured or flowing, and the verb describes a single outpouring.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r1.anchor: الدفق صب الماء ، يقال : دفقت الماء ، أي صببته وهو مدفوق

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj, attributing the view to Sībawayh, takes dāfiq as possessing a flow, like other nouns describing someone by what he has.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه ذو اندفاق ، كما يقال : دراع وفارس ونابل

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the object may be named with an active participle when used as an adjective; the Hijazis do this more, as in rādiyah meaning pleasing.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : وأهل الحجاز أفعل لهذا من غيرهم ، يجعلون المفعول فاعلا

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r4.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl defines the root as pouring out all at once and cites dāfiq khayr as an omen when a vessel spills.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r4.anchor: ذكر الخليل في الكتاب المنسوب إليه دفق الماء دفقا ودفوقا إذا انصب بمرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r5.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r5.claim: Quṭrub likewise defines the verb as flowing or pouring out.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r5.anchor: وفي كتاب قطرب : دفق الماء يدفق إذا انصب

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r6.claim: A further explanation is metaphor: the fluid's owner is called flowing because he is the one who emits it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r6.anchor: صاحب الماء لما كان دافقا أطلق ذلك على الماء على سبيل المجاز

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r13.speaker: صاحب القول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r13.claim: He further argues that dāfiq describes the man's fluid, and the following clause says this fluid exits from between loins and chest bones, supporting a male-only source.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r13.anchor: والذي يوصف بذلك هو ماء الرجل ، ثم عطف عليه بأن وصفه بأنه يخرج

RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r16.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r16.claim: A Prophetic report says the dominant man's fluid determines a boy and resemblance to his family, while the dominant woman's fluid determines resemblance to hers.
RAZI-FULL:v31p117/r16.anchor: إذا غلب ماء الرجل يكون الولد ذكرا ويعود شبه إليه وإلى أقاربه

STUDYQURAN:86:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:6/r1.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:86:6/r1.claim: Some understand the loins and pelvic arch as the man's and woman's respective parts, whose sperm and egg form the fetus.
STUDYQURAN:86:6/r1.anchor: are understood by some to refer to the respective parts of the man and the woman, whose sperm and egg form the fetus

TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.claim: He challenges resurrection deniers to inspect their creation from emitted, poured fluid; two unnamed poetic lines use tarāʾib with gold, saffron, neck, and chest imagery as linguistic evidence.
TAB-FULL:v24p296/r1.anchor: وقال آخر: [البحر الكامل] والزعفران على ترائبها … شرقا به اللبات والنحر

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.claim: The Angel of Death takes people at death, and God takes souls at death and sleep; angelic preservation can also mean preserving souls through writing their deeds.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.anchor: ولا ينافي هذا الوجه ظاهر آية الانفطار السابقة من أن حفظ الملائكة هو الكتابة

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.claim: An objection says absolute power cannot prove resurrection because recreating the very same human is impossible: a second body would be merely like, not identical to, the first.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.anchor: ومحصله أن إطلاق القدرة إنما ينفع فيما كان ممكنا لكن إعادة الإنسان بعينه محال فإن الإنسان المخلوق ثانيا مثل الانسان الدنيوي

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.claim: The answer is that personal identity resides in the preserved soul, not the body; when that soul joins a recreated body, it is the same person despite bodily similarity.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.anchor: وجه الاندفاع أن شخصية الشخص من الإنسان بنفسه لا ببدنه والنفس محفوظة فإذا خلق البدن وتعلقت به النفس كان هو الإنسان الدنيوي بشخصه

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r6.claim: Dafq is water pouring or flowing with force and speed; the gushing water is semen, and the phrase answers the implied question prompted by verse 5.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r6.anchor: الدفق تصبب الماء وسيلانه بدفع وسرعة والماء الدافق هو المني

TABATABAI:86:10-17/r17.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r17.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r17.claim: Al-Qummī identifies the emitted fluid as sperm that comes out forcefully.
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r17.anchor: وفيه في قوله تعالى { خلق من ماء دافق } قال النطفة التي تخرج بقوة

TABATABAI:86:10-17/r18.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r18.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r18.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the preceding report has a problem because it is elliptical and mursal.
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r18.anchor: أقول الرواية على إضمارها وإرسالها لا تخلو من شيء

TABRISI:86:1-17/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:1-17/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:86:1-17/r15.claim: Dafq is a forceful, abundant pouring; the reproductive fluid is called dāfiq for flowing and pouring out.
TABRISI:86:1-17/r15.anchor: والدفق صب الماء الكثير باعتماد قوي ومثله الدفع فالماء الذي يكون منه الولد

TABRISI:86:1-17/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:1-17/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:86:1-17/r16.claim: Another grammatical explanation takes ماء دافق to mean مدفوق, like a concealed secret or a pleasing life.
TABRISI:86:1-17/r16.anchor: وقيل: ماء دافق معناه مدفوق ومثله سر كاتم وعيشة راضية

TABRISI:86:2-9/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:86:2-9/r9.claim: The human is created from semen, poured into the woman’s womb and from which the child develops.
TABRISI:86:2-9/r9.anchor: أي من ماء مهراق في رحم المرأة يعني المني الذي يكون منه الولد عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:86:2-9/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:86:2-9/r10.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Hijaz usage often gives an active participle a passive sense, as in a concealed secret, they are made ready, and a sleeping night.
TABRISI:86:2-9/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: وأهل الحجاز يجعلون الفاعل بمعنى المفعول

THALABI:v10p179/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p179/r2.claim: “Dāfiq” is semen, poured into the womb; the active form carries a passive sense, as in “a concealed secret” and “a sleeping night.”
THALABI:v10p179/r2.anchor: خلق من ماء دافق أي مدفوق مصبوب في الرحم وهو المني، فاعل بمعنى مفعول كقولهم سر كاتم

THALABI:v10p179/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r3.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p179/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the active-form usage is supported by the word’s position at the ends of the surrounding verses.
THALABI:v10p179/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: أعان على ذلك أنها رؤوس الآيات التي معهن

THALABI:v10p179/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p179/r4.claim: “Dafq” means pouring; Arabs say a wave “tadaffaqa” or “indaffaqa” when it rises and falls.
THALABI:v10p179/r4.anchor: والدفق: الصب، تقول العرب للموج إذا علا وانحط: تدفق واندفق

THALABI:v10p179/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p179/r5.claim: The singular “water” means the two fluids of man and woman, from which the child is made, named one water because they mingle.
THALABI:v10p179/r5.anchor: وأراد من مائين: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة لأن الولد مخلوق منهما، ولكنه جعله ماء واحدا لامتزاجهما

BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.claim: Creation from matter untouched by life proves the Creator can restore the dead, indeed more readily by rational analogy, so people should prepare for recompense.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.anchor: من قدر على إنشائه من مواد لم تشم رائحة الحياة قط فهو قادر على إعادته بل أقدر على قياس العقل

BURSEVI:v10p309/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r5.claim: The phrase resumes the discourse as an answer to an implied question: from what was he created?
BURSEVI:v10p309/r5.anchor: خلق من مآء دافق} استئناف وقع جوابا عن استفهام مقدر كأنه قيل ممن خلق

BURSEVI:v10p309/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r6.claim: Dāfiq describes water poured with force and rapid flow; the text also gives a Persian gloss meaning “pouring water.”
BURSEVI:v10p309/r6.anchor: خلق من ماء ذي دفق وهو صب فيه دفع وسيلان بسرعة وبالفارسية ريزانيدن آب

BURSEVI:v10p309/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r7.claim: Although semen is poured rather than pouring, dāfiq is active in form through attribution of the verbal source to the described thing, regardless of its actual agency.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r7.anchor: وإنما أول بالنسبة لأن الصب لا يتصور من النطفة لظهور إنها مصبوبة لإصابة

BURSEVI:v10p309/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p309/r8.claim: Some interpret dāfiq passively as semen poured into the womb, like “a hidden secret” or “a pleasing life”; it denotes the mixture of the two fluids there.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أي مدفوق ومصبوب في الرحم نحو سر كاتم أي مكتوم وعيشة راضية أي مرضية

BURSEVI:v10p309/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r9.claim: The two fluids are named in the singular to emphasize their mixture, and the whole is described by a quality belonging to one of its parts.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r9.anchor: وللنظر إلى امتزاجهما عبر عنهما بصيغة الأفراد ووصف الماء الممتزج بالدافق من قبيل توصيف المجموع بوصف بعض أجزائه

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r4.claim: The Najmī interpretation reads human origin as the moisture of the All-Merciful’s Breath, and takes the flowing water as issuing from the fountain of divine love and creative effusion.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r4.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : خلق الإنسان من ماء رطوبة النفس الرحمني

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r5.claim: The Najmī gloss supports the Breath of the All-Merciful reading with the Prophet’s saying that he finds that breath coming from Yemen.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r5.anchor: عليه اسلام بقوله إني أجد نفس الرحمن من قبل اليمن

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r6.speaker: قوله تعالى
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r6.claim: The divine saying “I was a hidden treasure and loved to be known, so I created creation” is invoked to signify the fountain of love behind creation.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r6.anchor: المشار إليها بقوله تعالى : كنت كنزا مخفيا فأحببت أن أعرف فخلقت الخلق

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the verses: let the human consider his origin, created from a forcefully spurting water that comes from between backbone and breast.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r1.anchor: Meâl: Onun için insan düşünsün neden yaratıldı? (5). Bir atılgan sudan yaratıldı (6) ki sulb ile sîneler arasından çıkar (7).

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.claim: The passage warns of human weakness under surveillance while displaying God's power to create, preserve, elevate, and resurrect; reflection begins the effort to purify one's secrets and rise toward God rather than become proud.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r5.anchor: asıl siyak yalnız o hakāreti düşündürmek değil

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r6.claim: By naming the water dāfiq even at the beginning of creation, when it must reach the womb, the verse evokes an effortful motion that begins the human striving under discussion.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r6.anchor: nutfe hâlinde iken bile rahime intikal etmek için bir nevi cehd demek olan dıfk

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r7.speaker: Zeccâc (Sîbeveyh’ten naklen)
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj, citing Sībawayh, explains dāfiq as an attributive form meaning poured, like words such as tamir and laban.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r7.anchor: Zeccâc’ın Sîbeveyh’ten naklettiği üzereتامر ve لابن

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r8.speaker: Ferrâ
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the active form as a figurative attribution of the passive meaning; he says the people of the Hijaz often use this pattern in adjectival position.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r8.anchor: Ferrâ demiştir ki: “Sıfat mevkiinde bunu ehl-i Hicaz diğerlerinden daha çok yaparlar

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r9.claim: Elmalılı reports that al-Khalīl and Qutrub use dāfiq or dufūq for flowing or pouring forth.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r9.anchor: “dıfk” ve “dufuk” insibab mânasına da geldiği nakledilmiştir

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r10.claim: Whichever grammatical account is adopted, attributing dāfiq to the water evokes an effortful quality in it.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r10.anchor: suda bir cehd tasavvur ettirmek üzere dıfkın ona nisbet edilmiş olmasıdır

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r11.claim: Min marks origin and may also be partitive, which fits the sound hadith that a child does not come from all water: it is from a portion of it.

ELMALILI:86:5-7/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r12.claim: The indefinite form is contemptuous, giving the sense of a lowly or insignificant fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7/r12.anchor: Tenvin de tahkir içindir, mâ’-i mehîn mânasındadır

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r2.claim: Dāfiq may describe a part of the combined fluid and be applied to the whole; alternatively the woman's fluid also effuses into the womb and bears that quality.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r2.anchor: “dâfik” denilmesi de ba‘zın vasfını külle ıtlak kabîlindendir. Bir kısmı dâfik olmak hasebiyle mecmû‘a da o vasıf verilmiştir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r3.claim: Elmalılı says there is no question that the woman has a fluid called her semen in religious terminology and that both partners are involved in fertilization.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r3.anchor: kadının da bir suyu bulunduğunu ve buna şer‘an onun menisi tâbir olunduğunu ve alekanın husûlü için telkihte iki tarafın da alâkadar olduğunu

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r4.claim: He leaves open whether the woman's fluid carries vital material or is merely auxiliary, and whether the two contributions are both active or one active and one receptive.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r4.anchor: kadının suyu erkeğin nutfesi gibi hayâtî maddeyi ihtivâ ediyor mu yoksa mezi gibi bir mu‘âvin hizmeti yapmakla kalıyor mu?

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r5.speaker: bir kısım ulemâ
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r5.claim: Some scholars hold the man's fluid to be the primary material in procreation because Qur'anic descriptions progress from earth and clay to lowly water, nutfa, and dāfiq, without explicitly naming the woman's fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r5.anchor: bir kısım ulemâ, veledin husûlünde unsur-i aslî erkeğin suyu olduğuna kāil olmuş

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r6.speaker: diğer bir kısım ulemâ
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r6.claim: Other scholars count a female contribution because fertilization involves her material, later resemblance patterns reveal it, and the hadith links resemblance to which fluid prevails.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r6.anchor: Diğer taraftan ulûkun, yani telkīhin husûlünde kadından da bir maddenin inzimam ve iştirâki

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r7.claim: Elmalılı identifies the woman's contribution as the ovum or egg released from the ovary; calling it her semen reflects this female reproductive material.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r7.anchor: bu unsur kadının “bezr” veya “büyeyza” tâbir olunan ve telkih edilen yumurtacığıdır

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r8.claim: The hadith that a child comes from only part of the fluid applies to the woman's fluid as well: the relevant part is the ovum, not all her fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r8.anchor: لَيْسَ مِنْ كُلِّ الْمَاءِ يَكُونُ الْوَلَدُ hadisi

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.claim: A creation account in al-Muʾminūn lists nine stages: clay extract, drop, clinging form, lump, bones, flesh, new creation, death, and resurrection.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.anchor: birincisi “sülâletin min tîn”, ikincisi “nutfe”, üçüncüsü “aleka”, dördüncüsü “mudga”, beşincisi “izâm”, altıncısı “lahm”, yedincisi “halk-ı âhar”, sekizinci “mevt”, dokuzuncusu “ba‘s”tir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.claim: These verses condense the stages to recall God's preservation and power to resurrect; they begin with the most evident and immediate starting point for reflection, the spurting fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.anchor: bütün o merâtib مِمَّ خُلِقَ خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍۢ دَافِقٍۢ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌۭ mazmunlarında hulâsa edilerek

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.claim: Although the fluid is technically the second stage in the sequence described in 23:13, it is the clearest and nearest starting point for reflection and is often foregrounded in Qur'anic accounts.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r15.anchor: Fakat fi’l-hâl nazar yürütülmek için en zâhir ve en yakın olan mebde’ bu olduğu cihetle ekser âyetlerde evvelâ bu mebde’e nazar-ı dikkat celbolunmuştur

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.claim: Though modern embryology is commonly pursued for medicine rather than theology, studying human formation can infer the Creator's power and clarify moral, religious, and human duties, so Elmalılı proceeds under the command to reflect.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r17.anchor: yazılan eserler hep o gayeyi isdihdaf ettiklerinden dolayı ilâhiyât bakımından istidlâl ile meşgul olmazlar ise de

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.claim: God creates functions preserving both individuals and the species; reproduction is not governed by will alone, since that would disrupt the species’ increase.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r1.anchor: Allah sübhânehu ve teâlâ hıfz-ı şahs vezâifini îcad buyurduğu gibi hıfz-ı

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r2.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r2.claim: An innate drive and inward sensation in the reproductive organs impel procreation, much as inward hunger impels eating.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r2.anchor: tenâsül a‘zâlarında bulunan bâtınî ve vicdânî bir ihsas halk buyurmuştur. Bu a‘zâda o his, midede açlık hiss-i bâtınîsi menzilesindedir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r3.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r3.claim: The reproductive urge belongs to the organs themselves and is absent when they cannot function, including after castration in childhood.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r3.anchor: bu a‘zâ, fiilini îfâya kādir olmadığı zaman o his bulunmaz

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r4.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r4.claim: The sensation’s causes cannot be directly perceived; stored semen may contribute to desire, but abstinence is not its independent cause and habitual behavior also affects desire.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r4.anchor: Meninin vücûdunu ve havsalât-ı meneviyede meksini onun esbâbından olmak üzere zikretmişlerdir. Gerçi bunun ona mu‘în olduğunda şüphe yoktur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r5.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r5.claim: Women also experience sexual desire but do not emit seminal fluid; the brain, cerebellum, and imagination contribute to reproductive function.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r5.anchor: Bu his kadınlarda da bulunur, lâkin bunlarda ifrâz-ı menevî bulunmaz, muhh ve muhayha (dimağ ve dimağçe)den her birinin de hakikatte bu vazifenin mebâdîsinde dahli vardır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r6.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r6.claim: Male desire produces erection as blood enters and congests the erectile tissues, giving the penis the firmness needed for penetration.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r6.anchor: ihlîle iki mücevvef cisminde mütevezzi‘şiryanlar vâsıtasıyla büyük mikdarda kan indifâ‘eder, sonra bu kan ev‘iyede ihtikan eyler.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r7.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r7.claim: Excitation spreads through the male reproductive system and increases testicular secretion, analogously to increased salivation while chewing.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r7.anchor: Onda husûle gelen tenebbüh erkeğin sâir cihaz-ı tenasülîsine sirâyet eder, o vakit ünseyeynin ifrâzı çoğalır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r8.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r8.claim: Seminal vesicles contract and send semen through the ejaculatory ducts into the urethra; coordinated muscular contractions expel it forcefully.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r8.anchor: meni, kesretle havsalât-ı meneviyeye gelir, ondan da bu havsaleler tenebbüh eder, sonra tekabbuz edip onu kanât-ı kāzife vâsıtasıyla kanât-ı bevle def‘eder.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r9.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r9.claim: Male reproductive contractions propel semen into the vagina; the woman’s role is described as mainly preparatory, apart from barriers and constricting tissues that aid penetration.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r9.anchor: İşte bu birbirini tahrik eden kuvvetler sebebiyle meni mehbilde uzağa atılır, o duhul vaktinde kadının vazifesi bi’l-külliye kāsırdır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r10.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r10.claim: Women share pleasurable arousal; the vagina and clitoris become congested, and increasingly strong spasms affect the ovaries and tubes, leading to conception.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r10.anchor: Kadın da şehvet-i mülezzizenin severânında erkekle müşareket eder.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.claim: Intercourse is called the sole reproductive act from which reproduction arises.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r11.anchor: mâhiyeti böyle şerh olunan mücâma‘at, tevâlüdün neş’et eylediği yegâne fi‘l-i tenâsülîdir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.claim: Intercourse is only preparatory, bringing together and depositing materials from male and female regardless of whether will governs it.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r12.anchor: Lâkin irâde bunu gerek istîlâ etsin gerek etmesin, her hâlde bu fiil, techîzî (ihzârî) bir fiilden başka bir şey değildir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r13.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r13.claim: He distinguishes the semen that aids conception from madhy and wady, which merely lubricate and facilitate seminal fluid’s passage.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r13.anchor: Alûkun husûlüne mu‘în, ricâlden neş’et eden menidir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r14.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r14.claim: One reported theory says semen stops in the vagina, is absorbed there, and then travels through the circulation toward the ovary.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r14.anchor: Bazıları demiştir ki: Bu sâil-i menevî mehbilde tevakkuf eder. Çünkü bunların zu‘munca oradan massolunur, sonra deveran yollarından mebîze teveccüh eder.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r15.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r15.claim: A second reported theory says semen reaches the uterus, rises from it as vapor, and thereby reaches the ovary.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r15.anchor: Bazıları da demiştir ki rahime vâsıl olur, sonra buhar olarak su‘ûd eder, mebîze kadar varır da alûk hâsıl olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r16.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r16.claim: A third theory holds that semen reaches the uterus and passes through its two connecting tubes toward the ovaries.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r16.anchor: Ahîren bazıları da zan tarîkiyle demişlerdir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r17.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r17.claim: He favors the tube route as nearer the truth because conception completes in the ovaries and intercourse sends semen into the uterus.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r17.anchor: Zâhir budur ki bu re’y-i ahîr hakka akrebdir. Zira mâlum olmuştur ki alûk ancak mebîzlerde tamam olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r18.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r18.claim: He argues semen must reach the ovary itself: presumed seminal vapor alone is insufficient, tubes provide the route, and eggs and engorged tube ends have been observed there.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r18.anchor: farzolunan nesîm-i menevî alûkun husûlünde tek başına kifayet etmez, belki meninin mebîzlere bi-nefsihi müsademesi lâzımdır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r19.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r19.claim: He also argues that semen enters the uterus in intercourse and cites observations of ectopic pregnancy as evidence that conception completes in the ovaries.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#3/r19.anchor: Nitekim bu, rahim hâricinde hamilden tevazzuh eder. Şu da mâlum ve muhakkaktır ki meni rahime indifâ‘eder ve cimâ‘hâlinde kazîbin ucu labüd fevha-i rahimin vasatına vâsıl olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r1.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r1.claim: The ovaries are analogous to the testes: removing either causes infertility; ovaries grow at puberty, develop follicles, and regress at menopause.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r1.anchor: kadında iki mebîz, erkekte husyeteyn menzilesindedir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r2.speaker: Bu fennin ulemâsının kısm-ı a‘zamı
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r2.claim: Most specialists regard the small follicles visible at puberty as the source of the ovum.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r2.anchor: Bu fennin ulemâsının kısm-ı a‘zamı bu havsalaları bezrenin menşe’i itibar etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r3.speaker: Tecribecilerin büyük bir kısmı
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r3.claim: Experimenters reported finding an egg in an ovarian follicle after conception; it grows, separates, enters a tube, and proceeds to the uterus or its equivalent.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r3.anchor: küçük habbeler içinde bir habbe bulmuşlardır

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r4.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r4.claim: Animals differ in whether the egg is laid outside or deposited in an internal womb; this divides them into egg-laying and live-bearing groups.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r4.anchor: Bu vazifedeki bu ihtilâftan dolayı hayvânât iki büyük fırkaya inkisam eder: yumurta ile tevâlüd eden hayvanlar, hayy mevcûdât doğuran hayvanlar.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r5.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r5.claim: The observed egg that separates from the ovary and remains in the uterus is established as originating in the female.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r5.anchor: bu bezrenin kadından neş’et ettiği muhakkak olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r6.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r6.claim: The actual generative process is too slight for the senses to observe; semen’s contact with the ovary is ordinarily necessary.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r6.anchor: Bu vazifede fi‘l-i uzvî pek cüz’îdir. Onun için havâssımız

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r7.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r7.claim: Because fertilization depends on coordinated vital properties of the organs and differs from chemical or physical processes, he classifies it as a biological function.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r7.anchor: Bu vazife kimyevî ve fizikî fiillere muhalif olduğu cihetle bunu hayâtî vezâif-i uzviyeden addetmemiz lâzimedendir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r8.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r8.claim: Researchers have produced only conjectures about fertilization’s mechanism, which he nevertheless summarizes rather than discarding.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r8.anchor: ancak zannî bir sözden başka bir şey elde edememişlerdir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r9.speaker: Birinci kavil
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r9.claim: The first theory places the embryo already in the female ovary, formed there by an action specific to that organ.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r9.anchor: Bu haysiyetten mebîzdeki bezre (yumurtacık) bu ‘kâin-i cedîd’in cümlesini muhtevî olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r10.speaker: Birinci kavil
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r10.claim: In this theory the ovum contains the whole potential being, like an unfertilized hen’s egg, but needs male semen to become capable of life.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r10.anchor: bu ‘kâin-i cedîd’in cümlesini muhtevî olur. Ancak bu kâin tek başına hayâta ihtisâsı bulunmamak haysiyetiyle bâkir tavuk yumurtası gibidir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r11.speaker: Birinci kavil
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r11.claim: The first theory explains resemblance and inherited disease through semen imprinting the soft ovum like a seal marks soft wax; greater male effort supposedly increases paternal resemblance.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r11.anchor: Bu seyyâlin o yumuşak bezrede tesiri mührün yumuşak mumda tesirine benzer ki mum o eseri hıfzeder kalır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r12.speaker: İkinci kavil; Hipokrat ve Calinos
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r12.claim: The older Hippocratic and Galenic theory mixes male and female semen in the womb; some later authors also hold it.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r12.anchor: İkinci kavil; iki meninin: erkek menisi ile dişi menisinin rahimde ihtilâtı hakkında söyledikleri tarîkat-ı kadîmedir ki Hipokrat’ın ve Calinos’un

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r13.speaker: İkinci kavil
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r13.claim: This account says each parent’s organs emit particles that arrange around an inner bodily mold, explaining children’s resemblance to their parents.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r13.anchor: ve binyenin esasını teşkil eyleyen bir bâtın kalıbı etrafında saflanıp dizilirler.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r14.speaker: bezriyyûn ‘tohumcular’
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r14.claim: The cited account calls the seed theory the best of the proposed routes, while noting that it contains several different views.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r14.anchor: Kavl-i sâlis; bezriyyûn ‘tohumcular’ tarîkatıdır ki ahsen-i turuktur. Bunda da muhtelif akvâl vardır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r15.speaker: mütekaddimîn; Pythagoras
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r15.claim: An older seed theory places the joining of the two seeds in the womb through a subtle nervous element, as Pythagoras held, or through magnetism or seminal fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r15.anchor: mütekaddimîn şunu ihtiyar etmişlerdir: Nutfeteynin ihyâsı rahimde olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r16.speaker: Müteahhirînin büyük bir kısmı
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r16.claim: Most later proponents locate fertilization in the ovary but disagree whether semen arrives by absorption and blood circulation, vapor, magnetism, electricity, or intercourse-induced disturbance.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#4/r16.anchor: ictimâ‘ancak mebîzde olur ve el’an müteahhirînin büyük bir kısmının re’yi budur. Ancak bunlar da şunda ihtilâf etmektedirler.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r1.speaker: Kiminin re’yince
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r1.claim: One animalcule theory says fertilization occurs in the uterus without the ovum participating.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r1.anchor: Bunlardan kiminin re’yince telkih, rahimde bezrin müşareketi olmadan hâsıl olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r2.speaker: Kiminin re’yince
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r2.claim: Another version says animalcules draw ovarian follicles into the uterus, where they accumulate and are fertilized.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r2.anchor: Kiminin re’yince de mezkur hayvancıklar mebîzin havsalalarını rahimde beraber terâküm etmek için cezbederler de telkih, rahimde hâsıl olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r3.speaker: Kimi
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r3.claim: A third version supposes that one animalcule draws an ovum into the uterus, opens a small passage, and enters it to fertilize it.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r3.anchor: Kimi de şöyle farzetmiştir: Bu hayvancıklardan birisi rahimde bezrini cezbeder de ondan küçük bir menfez açarak içine dâhil olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r4.speaker: Prikus ve Domas
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r4.claim: Prikus and Domas, returning to Hippocrates and Aristotle, place fertilization in the uterus, citing animalcules found there rather than in the tubes or ovaries.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r4.anchor: Prikus ve Domas, Bukrat’ın ve Aristoteles’in re’yine rücû‘ederek tecvîf-i rahim, meclis-i telkih olduğunu ihtiyar etmişler ve bunu birtakım umûr ile tekid eylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r5.speaker: Prikus ve Domas
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r5.claim: They argue that an ovum needs a mucous coating acquired while traveling from the ovary through a tube, and report no observed artificial fertilization of an ovum taken directly from the ovary.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r5.anchor: Bir de bezir ihtilâttan evvel bir tabaka-i muhâtiye ile gılıflanmaya muhtaçtır. Bunu ise mebîzden rahime giderken nefîrden alır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r6.speaker: Ruviş ve bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r6.claim: Against the uterine theory, Ruviş and others report finding generative semen in a woman’s tube and in female animals, including dogs and cattle.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r6.anchor: Ruviş madde-i müvellideyi, yani meniyi zâniye bir karının -ki o sırada kocası öldürmüştü- nefîrinde bulmuştur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r7.claim: The account analogizes human fertilization to frogs’ eggs, which require immersion in thick mucous fluid before fertilization can occur.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r7.anchor: Kurbağaların yumurtasını telkih ancak önce koyu bir dühn-i muhâtîye[^54] batırılmakla mümkin olduğu bizce mâlum bulunduğu cihetle kadınlarda husûlünü de ona kıyas edebiliriz.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r8.claim: The account notes claims of tubal and ectopic pregnancies and an embryo seen spanning tube and ovary, while acknowledging these observations may not be established.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r8.anchor: Ne nefirî bir hamlin vücûdu ve ne nısfını nefîrde nısfını mebîzde

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r9.speaker: Prikus ve Domas
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r9.claim: The account suggests their ovarian eggs judged unfertilizable may have been damaged by the instruments used to remove them.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r9.anchor: zâhir oluyor ki onlar onu mebîzden kuvvetle ayırırlarken âletler onda mutlak bir tegayyür ihdas etmiştir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r10.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r10.claim: The actual fertilization mechanism remains unknown; the observed account is that a mature follicle swells, thins, ruptures during intercourse, releases an ovum, and the ovum enters the tube.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r10.anchor: Mebîzin hâvî olduğu havsalalardan birisi büluğdan sonra sür‘atle büyür

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r11.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r11.claim: After the follicle ruptures, its wound heals slowly and leaves a pitted or sunken mark called the ‘small body.’
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r11.anchor: ‘cism-i asgar’ denilen asıl bu pürüz veya eserdir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r12.speaker: Bu fennin ulemâsı
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r12.claim: Specialists say the competing accounts of the ovarian structures require renewed investigation.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r13.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r13.claim: One observer reports large yellow ovarian masses and varied internal appearances; their rupture can leave a deep cavity, and more than one may occur for an ovum.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r13.anchor: Ben kadınların mebîzinde hatta telkihten evvel sararmış bir kütle hatta soğan hacminde ba‘zı da fındık gibi kütleler müşahede ettim.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r14.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r14.claim: Observations show that after fertilization an ovum separates from the ovary and develops into an organism resembling the one that generated it, but nothing beyond this is known.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r14.anchor: Müşahedelerden sâbit olan ancak budur. Bundan ziyadesi bilinmiyor.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r15.speaker: Muhammed b. Ahmed el-İskenderânî
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r15.claim: Semen leaving the male contains a small milky fluid attributed to the prostate and a thick white fluid attributed to the testes that carries the life matter.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r15.anchor: Birisi lebenîdir, azdır, bunun aslı prostat (kestanecik) denilen guddeye nisbet olunur. İkincisi beyaz, koyu, gıreviyyü’l-manzar (ak tutkal manzarasında)dır.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r16.speaker: Tahkik ettiklerine göre
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r16.claim: The reported composition assigns 112.5 parts water, 7.5 animal mucus, and 1.25 soda among 125 parts of semen.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r16.anchor: insan menisinden her yüz yirmi beş cüz, yüz on iki buçuk cüz suyu yedi buçuk cüz muhâtî

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r17.speaker: Tahkik ettiklerine göre
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r17.claim: The same analysis adds 3.75 parts phosphate of lime, mucous matter, volatile matter, and sulfur.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r17.anchor: üç buçuk ve rubu‘cüz fosfat kilsi, yani yanmış kemik gibi bir türâbı ihtivâ eder. Onda bunlardan mâ‘adâ bir mâdde-i muhâtıye ve bir mâdde-i tayyâre ve kükürt de bulunur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r18.claim: Semen liquefies into a watery fluid after about 20–25 minutes for an unknown reason; mild warmth suffices, while stronger heating decomposes it and releases ammonia.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r18.anchor: Meni bir kabda örtülü veya örtüsüz bırakıldığı vakit yirmi yirmi beş dakika sonra su gibi incelir ve bunun sebebi mâlum değildir.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r19.claim: In hot dry air semen thickens and forms calcium-phosphate crystals; in hot humid air it yellows, turns acidic, develops a foul fish-like odor, and molds.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r19.anchor: eğer hava hâr ve kuru ise koyulaşır ve katılır ve onda fosfat kils billûrâtı peydâ olur.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r20.claim: Semen does not dissolve in hot or cold water until diluted; dropped into water it sinks, partly coagulates and dissolves, and the remainder disperses like cotton fibers.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r20.anchor: Meninin havâssındandır ki ne sıcak ne de soğuk suda cıvıtmadan evvel erimez. İnsandan infisâli hâlinde meni bir suya düşerse kabın dibine iner ve biraz in‘ikad eyler sonra bir miktarı erir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r21.claim: After filtration and heating, the semen extract gives its characteristic odor and a slightly yellow pearly appearance; further processing leaves material said to resemble meat extract, and its ash contains soda.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#5/r21.anchor: süzüntü “hammâm-ı mâriye” üzerinde kuruyuncaya kadar teshin edilirse ondan bir râyiha kokar ki meninin kendine mahsus râyihasıdır. Ve biraz sarıya mâil lü’lüî bir hey’et iktisab eder.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r1.claim: Male semen is secreted in the testes, passes through fine ducts to the seminal vesicles, then travels through the spermatic and ejaculatory passages.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r1.anchor: Meni husyelerde ifraz olunup ev‘iye-i âtiye denilen ev‘iye-i mahsûsasından te‘âkub üzere geçer, habl-i menevî kanât-ı nâkılesinden havsalaya gider

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r2.claim: Female fluid is a light, transparent, pure secretion from the vaginal walls and nearby labia; Elmalılı says it lacks the life present in male semen.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r2.anchor: Dişinin suyu; evvelâ biraz lüzûceti bulunan bir sâil-i mâyi‘dir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r3.claim: God designed the female passages so that fluid release brings pleasure and awakens her reproductive organs for fertilization of the ovum.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r3.anchor: kudret-i ilâhiye fevhe-i fercde o ev‘iye-i intısâbiyeyi yaratmış ve bu sâilin nüzûlünü tam bir lezzet ile müterâfık kılmıştır

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r4.claim: The paired ovaries resemble the male testes and contain small follicles with viscous fluid, which Elmalılı cautiously identifies as embryonic seeds.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r4.anchor: Sâniyen, erkekteki husyeler menzilesinde olan hacimleri fındık gibi ve hey’etleri lîfî, basık beyzî şekilde bulunan iki mebîz dahi lüzûcetli bir sâili muhtevî

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r5.claim: The fallopian tubes attach to the uterus, surround the ovaries with their fringed ends, and carry the ovarian material toward the womb.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r5.anchor: Rahimin iki cânibi üzerinde a‘lâdan her biri bir cânibde iki sakbe vardır. Bunlara rahim boruları denilen iki

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r6.claim: Elmalılı describes the ovarian follicles as preformed seeds capable of later growth through male semen; the tubes convey them to the womb.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r6.anchor: bilâhare erkek menisinden nümüvvü kābil olmak üzere önce tekvin olunmuş birer bezr diye zan ve telakkī olunmaktadır

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r7.claim: This account accords with juristic descriptions: male semen is white, thick, and spurting, while female fluid is thin, yellow, and non-spurting.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r7.anchor: fıkıhta erkek menisi beyaz, galîz ve dıfıklı, kadın menisi rakīk, sarı ve dıfıksız olur diye târif olunması da bu îzâhât ile mütenâsibdir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r8.claim: The child comes from the two fluids issuing between loins and breastbones; Elmalılı says the female contributes a vessel-like element.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r8.anchor: Bu suretle veled, sulb ile terâib arasından çıkan iki suyun mecmû‘undan husûle gelir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r9.claim: Male spurting semen contains many sperm cells; each, after growth, may develop into a world-like being and generate the nervous system.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r9.anchor: Erkeğin dâfik olan menisi birçok miktarda habbât-ı meneviyeyi ihtivâ eyler ki her biri nümüvvünden sonra neş’et ettiği kâine şebîh kâinat olmak mümkin

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r10.claim: Human development proceeds from the nutfa to the alaqa, an attached drop, then to a morsel, bones, flesh, and a seventh stage of renewed creation before birth.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r10.anchor: İnsan bu vechile nutfe mertebesinden üçüncü mertebe olan aleka tavrına geçer ki o tutmuş olan nutfe olup cidden muhtelif zamanlarda

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r11.speaker: Ulemâ
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r11.claim: Scholars hold that the dark original point in the transparent embryonic fluid adheres to its membranes.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r11.anchor: bu nokta ulemânın re’yine göre lifaflarına mültesıktır

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r12.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r12.claim: Others place the dark original point in the middle of the fluid rather than attached to its membranes.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r12.anchor: Bazılarının re’yince ise o sâilin vasatında sâbihtir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r13.speaker: Bukrat
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r13.claim: Hippocrates says that after six days a small transparent sphere forms in the fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r13.anchor: Bukrat altı günde sâilin vasatında şeffaf bir küre-i sağīre olur demiş

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r14.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r14.claim: Some say the embryonic form can be observed only after fifteen days.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r14.anchor: bazıları da ancak on beş günden sonra müşahede olunabileceğini söylemiştir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r15.claim: Elmalılı says implantation takes some days, but the duration has not been established across animal species; reports give rabbits three days and dogs six to eight.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r15.anchor: Zâhir olan tavşanda üç gün, köpeklerde altıdan yediye

ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r16.speaker: Bazıları
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r16.claim: Some say the human form begins after thirty-five days, when it is about the size of a bee; Elmalılı notes that other accounts exist.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#6/r16.anchor: bazıları ceninde şekl-i beşerînin ancak otuz beş günde başladığına

ELMALILI:86:5-7#7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#7/r8.claim: The fluid is specifically called “spurting” because its emission and point of passage during intercourse depend on the region between the woman’s loins and breastbones.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#7/r8.anchor: Onun için burada da “mâ-i dâfik” mutlak bırakılmayıp bu şarta işaret için bu sıfatla tavsif olunmuştur

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.claim: Attention to human creation from a drop helps people recognize themselves and the deliberate Creator, an especially evident proof of divine power.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r1.anchor: Bu vechile insanın nutfeden hilkatine nazar-ı dikkati celbetmenin fâidesi de pek büyüktür

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.claim: The body’s extraordinary composition and the transformation of a lowly substance like mucus into a rational, remembering, aspiring human prove the Creator’s existence and power.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r2.anchor: insanın bedeninde terkîbât-ı acîbe ekserdir. Binâen‘aleyh onun sümük gibi hakir ve basit görünen bir maddeden halkı kādir-i muhtârın vücûduna ve kudretine edeldir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r4.claim: People continually observe birth in their children and other animals, making this evidence for the deliberate Creator especially strong.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.claim: Human creation also proves resurrection: the Creator gathers scattered components, forms them, and breathes in a soul, so He can gather them again after death.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#8/r5.anchor: mevt ile o eczânın teferrukundan sonra onları cem‘e ve evvelki gibi düzgün mahluklar yapmaya kādir olduğunu itiraf elbette vâcib olur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.claim: Those denying resurrection and the afterlife are urged to learn from their own creation and judge whether resurrection after death is possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.anchor: Öldükten sonra dirilmeyi ve âhiret hayatını inkâr eden insanın, kendi yaratılışına bakarak ibret alması ve öldükten sonra yeniden dirilmeyi (ba‘s), dolayısıyla âhiret gerçeğini buna göre değerlendirmesi istenmektedir

BURHAN:v2p283/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p283/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p283/r9.claim: The active participle دافق is used with passive meaning: مدفوق.
BURHAN:v2p283/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ من ماء دافق ﴾ اي مدفوق

QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.claim: The gushing fluid comes from the father's loins and the mother's nurturing.
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r8.anchor: يخرج من صلب الأب ، وتربية الأم

QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.claim: Reflection on human origin urges inference to God's complete power, knowledge, and will.
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r9.anchor: يحثه على النظر والاستدلال حتى يعرف كمال قدرته وعلمه وإرادته

BURHAN:v1p367/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p367/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p367/r5.claim: He recommends separating identical consecutive words with a pause, illustrated by خلق at the end of 86:5 and start of 86:6, and by 9:108.
BURHAN:v1p367/r5.anchor: اجتناب تكرير اللفظة الواحدة فى القرآن تكريرا من غير فصل

ITQAN:v3p269/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p269/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p269/r6.claim: An active participle can occur where a passive sense is intended, as in a life that is pleasing and water that is poured forth.
ITQAN:v3p269/r6.anchor: وقوع ( فاعل ) موقع ( مفعول ) نحو ﴿ في عيشة راضية ﴾

KHATTABI:v1p69/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p69/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p69/r1.claim: The imitator wrongly uses “faʿala” for the favor of pregnancy, since the expression typically evokes punishment; wording such as “showed kindness” or “bestowed favor” fits the intended meaning.
KHATTABI:v1p69/r1.anchor: فإن أول ما غلط به هذا الجاهل أنه وضع كلمة الانتقام في موضع كلمة الإنعام

FARRA:v3p254#2/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p254#2/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p254#2/r9.claim: Hijazi usage readily gives an active form a passive sense when it functions adjectivally, as in سر كاتم, وهم ناصب, ليل نائم, and عيشة راضية; the verse endings also favor it.
FARRA:v3p254#2/r9.anchor: أن يجعلوا المفعول فاعلا إذا كان في مذهب نعت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r5.claim: Arabic may put the object in active form: dāfiq means madfūq (ejected); similarly ʿāṣim means protected, rāḍiya pleasing, and mubṣira made clear by it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r5.anchor: ومنه أن يجيء المفعول به على لفظ الفاعل: كقوله سبحانه: لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r6.claim: Dāfiq means madfūq, 'ejected'; it is an active form with passive sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r6.anchor: وقوله: خلق من ماء دافق (6) [الطارق: 6] ، أي مدفوق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r7.claim: Arabic also calls a night sleeping and a secret concealing, using an active participle for the object's state or effect.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r7.anchor: والعرب تقول: ليل نائم، وسر كاتم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r8.speaker: وعلة الجرمي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r8.claim: Waʿila al-Jurmi's line calls the day aḥmas fājir, glossed as a hard day in which force is used.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r8.anchor: قال وعلة الجرمي : ولما رأيت الخيل تترى أثايجا ... علمت بأن اليوم أحمس فاجر أي يوم صعب مفجور فيه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p179/r9.claim: The author begins to note that faʿīl can mean mufʿil, but this excerpt supplies no example.

NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.claim: مِمَّ contracts from مما; the alif is deleted because ما is interrogative, and the question is complete.
NAHHAS:v5p197/r11.anchor: الأصل مما حذفت الألف لأنها استفهام وتم الكلام

NAHHAS:v5p197/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p197/r12.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
NAHHAS:v5p197/r12.claim: Al-Kisai and al-Farra take دافق to mean مدفوق, a passive sense expressed with an active participle.
NAHHAS:v5p197/r12.anchor: قول الكسائي والفراء أن معنى دافق مدفوق

NAHHAS:v5p197/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p197/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p197/r13.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects the active-for-passive explanation as false and non-analogical: if valid, ضارب could mean مضروب.
NAHHAS:v5p197/r13.anchor: قال أبو جعفر فاعل بمعنى مفعول فيه بطلان البيان ولا يصح ولا ينقاس ولو جاز هذا لجاز ضارب بمعنى مضروب

NAHHAS:v5p197/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p197/r14.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v5p197/r14.claim: The Basrans analyze دافق as a relational adjective, as in an un-attributed poem’s ناصب and another’s نبال; both lines illustrate the adjective pattern.
NAHHAS:v5p197/r14.anchor: والقول عند البصريين أنه على النسب كما قال

SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r1.claim: دافق may be an active participle with passive meaning, like سيل مفعم and, on one analysis, حجابا مستورا.
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r1.anchor: قيل: فاعل بمعنى مفعول كعكسه في قولهم: " سيل مفعم "

SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r2.claim: Alternatively, دافق is a relational adjective meaning possessing a gush or flow.
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r2.anchor: وقيل: دافق على النسب، أي: ذي دفق أو اندفاق

SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says water can be called دافق because some of it pushes other portions; thus either دافق or مدفوق can describe it.
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " يصح أن يكون الماء دافقا؛ لأن بعضه يدفق بعضا، أي: يدفعه فمنه دافق، ومنه مدفوق

SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r4.claim: دفق means pouring, and the verb is transitive.

SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads مدفوق, apparently explaining the intended sense.
SAMIN-DURR:86:6/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد ابن علي " مدفوق " وكأنه فسر المعنى

ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r1.claim: He glosses dāfiq as coming from above.

ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه وأصحابه
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r2.claim: Sibawayh and his associates derive dāfiq by relation to effusion: it means water possessing an effusion.
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r2.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه وأصحابه أن معناه النسب إلى الاندفاق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r1.speaker: المفسرون
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r1.claim: Some exegetes take the active participle as passive in several Qur’anic phrases, including دافق as مدفوق and راضية as مرضية.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r1.anchor: قسم من المفسرين يرون أحياناً في الإستعمالات القرآنية أن اسم الفاعل يكون بمعنى اسم المفعول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r2.claim: The surface active form and its meaning can stand; دافق need not be reinterpreted as مدفوق.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r2.anchor: ومن الممكن تخريجها على صورتها الظاهرة ويبقى المعنى وليس بالضرورة أن نؤوّل كلمة دافق لمعنى مدفوق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r3.speaker: المفسرون
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r3.claim: Other exegetical analyses also preserve the active and passive forms and their meanings as sound readings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر المفسرون آراء أخرى تؤكد الإقرار على المعاني والصيغ اسم الفاعل واسم المفعول ويستقيم المعنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r4.claim: A verbal noun in the Qur’an can sometimes carry the meaning of an active or passive participle, as with حَلْق meaning مخلوق.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p604/r4.anchor: المصدر قد يأتي بمعنى اسم الفاعل أو اسم المفعول في القرآن مثل كلمة (حلق) فهي تأتي بمعنى مخلوق أحياناً

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.claim: Human origin is a bodily fluid, not a rare substance beyond God's reach; since He made a living person from it, He can recreate him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.anchor: he is made from a drop of fluid which emanates from his own body.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p448#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p448#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p448#2/r3.claim: دفق الماء means pouring water; ماء دافق is an attributed construction, and the root is also used in a curse wishing death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p448#2/r3.anchor: دفق الماء يدفقه دفقا: صبه، وماء دافق على النسب، ويقال: دفق الله روحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.claim: Because every soul has a guardian, people should reflect on their first creation, know the Creator can restore and requite them, and act so their recorder contains what pleases them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر أن كل نفس عليها حافظ، أتبع ذلك بوصية الإنسان بالنظر في أول نشأته الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r3.claim: The answer is semen from man and woman, described as one water after they mingle and unite in the womb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r3.anchor: وجواب الاستفهام ما بعده وهو: خلق من ماء دافق، وهو مني الرجل والمرأة لما امتزجا في الرحم واتحدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r4.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads دافق as passive in the sense of مدفوق.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r4.anchor: ودافق قيل: هو بمعنى مدفوق، وهي قراءة زيد بن علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r5.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r5.claim: They analyze the form as an attributive construction meaning ذي دفق, like كلبن وتامر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r5.anchor: وعند الخليل وسيبويه: هو على النسب، كلا بن وتامر، أي ذي دفق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says sticky or viscous, apparently a quality rather than a lexical definition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: بمعنى دافق لزج، وكأنه أطلق عليه وصفه لا أنه موضوع في اللغة لذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the water is dāfiq because its parts push one another; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because دفق means pouring, not mutual pushing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والدفق: دفع الماء بعضه ببعض، تدفق الوادي والسيل إذا جاء يركب بعضه بعضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Ibn ʿAṭiyya builds on تدفق, but established دفق means pouring and does not mean one part pushing another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p451/r8.anchor: وركب قوله هذا على تدفق، وتدفق لازم دفقته فتدفق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.claim: The clause begins a fresh answer to the implied question, From what was he created?
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.anchor: استئناف وقع جوابا عن استفهام مقدر كأنه قيل مم خلق فقيل خلق من ماء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.claim: Alusi calls it imprecise to attach this answer directly to the preceding command to consider; the answer is syntactically detached from that clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.anchor: وظاهر كلام بعض الأجلة أنه جواب الاستفهام المذكور مع تعلق الجار بينظر وفيه مسامحة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.claim: Dafq means pouring with force and flowing rapidly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.anchor: والدفق صب فيه دفع وسيلان بسرعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads dafiq with the passive sense, meaning poured out.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.anchor: وقد قرأ بذلك زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r5.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r5.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh take dafiq as a relational adjective meaning possessed of a flow, applicable to both agent and patient.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r5.anchor: وقال الخليل وسيبويه هو على النسب كلا بن وتامر أي ذي دفق وهو صادق على الفاعل والمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r6.claim: One explanation treats dafiq as an active participle metaphorically predicated of water, transferring the person's action to it for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r6.anchor: وقيل هو اسم فاعل وإسناده إلى الماء مجاز وأسند إليه ما لصاحبه مبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r7.speaker: السكاكي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r7.claim: Al-Sakkaki's analysis calls the expression an implicit and imaginative metaphor; an explicit-metaphor analysis pictures successive drops as pushing one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r7.anchor: أو هو استعارة مكنية وتخييلية كما ذهب إليه السكاكي و مصرحة بجعله دافقا لأنه لتتابع قطراته كأنه يدفق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya glosses daf q as pushing: a valley or torrent flows with one part riding over another, and portions of the fluid push each other.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r8.anchor: وقد فسر ابن عطية الدفق بالدفع فقال الدفق دفع الماء بعضه ببعض يقال تدفق الوادي والسيل إذا جاء يركب بعضه بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that daf q meaning push is not established in Arabic; the attested sense is pouring.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r9.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان بأن الدفق بمعنى الدفع غير محفوظ في اللغة بل المحفوظ أنه الصب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r10.speaker: الليث
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r10.claim: Al-Layth gives dafaqa the sense of pouring out all at once, making dafiq simply flowing; Alusi notes this usage is unique to al-Layth in the lexicons he cites.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r10.anchor: ونقل عن الليث أن دفق بمعنى انصب بمرة فدافق بمعنى منصب فلا حاجة إلى التأويل وتعقب بأنه مما تفرد به الليث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r11.claim: Although human creation involves male and female fluids, the verse calls their mixture in the womb one water; Jesus' creation without that mixture is extraordinary.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r11.anchor: لأن المراد به الممتزج من الماءين في الرحم وبالأمتزاج صارا ماء واحدا ووصفه بالدفق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r12.claim: The fluid is called flowing either with reference to the male component alone or to both components, since the woman's fluid also flows toward the womb.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p96#2/r12.anchor: قيل باعتبار أحد جزئيه وهو مني الرجل وقيل باعتبار كليهما ومني المرأة دافق أيضا إلى الرحم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r2.claim: The dāfiq water is semen poured into the womb; dāfiq means poured, though its active form carries a passive sense, as in “a pleasing life,” meaning one made pleasing (69:21).
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r2.anchor: مدفوق أي مصبوب في الرحم، وهو المني، فاعل بمعنى مفعول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r3.claim: The singular water refers to both male and female fluids, since the child is formed from both and they mix together.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394/r3.anchor: وأراد ماء الرجل وماء المرأة، لأن الولد مخلوق منهما، وجعله واحدا لامتزاجهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r1.claim: This answers the preceding question; the fluid is one that gushes forcefully, and means the mixture of two fluids in the womb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r1.anchor: وهو صعب فيه دفع والمراد الممتزج من الماءين في الرحم

BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r2.claim: The expression means fluid possessing a forceful gush.
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:6-7/r2.anchor: بمعنى ذي دفق، وهو صعب فيه دفع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.claim: The sūra’s purpose is to exalt the Qurʾān’s truthfulness about the reward of believers and punishment of disbelievers at Judgment, when every hidden secret is exposed and recorded.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.anchor: في يوم القيامة حين تبلى السرائر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.claim: The name al-Ṭāriq best signals this true promise when one reflects on the oath and the matter sworn to.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.anchor: واسمها الطارق أدل ما فيها على هذا الموعود الصادق بتأمل القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r6.claim: The origin should command full attention because recognizing it brings eternal happiness, but human weakness and distraction make God explain the answer.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r7.claim: Human creation is easy after Adam was made from earth and Eve from his rib.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r7.anchor: أي الإنسان على أيسر وجه وأسهله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r8.claim: Dāfiq describes fluid that gushes with force as if it propelled itself, though the emission is attributed figuratively to the man; dafaq means pouring with a thrust.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r9.claim: The singular fluid rather than two waters points to the man’s and woman’s fluids mixing so thoroughly in the womb that they become one.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r9.anchor: يجتمعان في الرحم ويمتزجان أشد امتزاج

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r2.speaker: الأعمش
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash says the man’s fluid forms bones and nerves, while the woman’s fluid forms flesh and blood.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r2.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق وابن المنذر عن الأعمش قال: يخلق العظام والعصب من ماء الرجل ويخلق اللحم والدم من ماء المرأة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r11.claim: دافق means issuing forcefully and swiftly; it most commonly describes a man’s semen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r11.anchor: خارج بقوة وسرعة والأشهر أنه يقال على نطفة الرجل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r12.claim: Some linguists derive دافق as an active participle from intransitive دفق; most reject an intransitive use and treat it as passive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p261/r12.anchor: وقال الجمهور : لا يستعمل دفق قاصرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r6.speaker: كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r6.claim: Many say دافق means مدفوق, poured out.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r6.anchor: ودافق، قال كثير: هو بمعنى: مدفوق،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r7.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r7.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh take دافق as relational, meaning possessing a gush; its parts push together.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465/r7.anchor: وقال الخليل وسيبويه: هو على النسب أي ذي دفق، والدفق: دفق الماء بعضه إلى بعض،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says dāfiq means madfūq, passive in sense; Arabic sometimes uses an active form with passive meaning, as in the cited expressions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r1.anchor: قال الفراء معناه مدفوق كقول العرب سر كاتم وهم ناصب وليل نائم وعيشة راضية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج وسيبويه وأصحابه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj attributes to Sībawayh's school the view that dāfiq is an adjective of attribution, meaning water characterized by flowing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p82#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج ومذهب سيبويه وأصحابه أن معناه النسب إلى الاندفاق والمعنى من ماء ذي اندفاق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r2.claim: The flowing, spurting fluid is semen; it issues from both man and woman, and by God’s permission the two together produce the child.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375/r2.anchor: يعني: المني؛ يخرج دفقا من الرجل ومن المرأة، فيتولد منهما الولد بإذن الله

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7932/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7932/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7932/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said everything was created from water, then prescribed greeting people, feeding them, keeping kin ties and night prayer as deeds leading to peaceful entry into Paradise.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7932/r1.anchor: فقال: " كل شيء خلق من ماء "

MUSNAD-AHMAD:10399/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10399/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10399/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said everything was created from water, then prescribed greeting people, kind speech, keeping kin ties and night prayer as deeds leading to peaceful entry into Paradise.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10399/r1.anchor: فقال: " كل شيء خلق من ماء "

JISHUMI:v10p7367/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r5.claim: The verse indicates that seminal-fluid components contribute to the child, even though other components join them before the child becomes alive.
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r5.anchor: ويدل قوله: (من ماء دافق) أن أجزاء النطفة في الولد، وإن انضم إليها أجزاء أخر حتى يصير الولد ولدا حيا،

JISHUMI:v10p7367/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r6.claim: Scholars disagree whether the child is created from the two fluids or from the man’s fluid alone.
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r6.anchor: واختلفوا، قيل: يخلق من الماءين، وقيل: من ماء الرجل،

JISHUMI:v10p7367/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r7.claim: Remembering one’s humble origin and eventual fate after death should prevent arrogance.
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r7.anchor: فإذا علم الإنسان ما خلق منه وما صار بعد الموت إليه لم يلتمس مورد الكبر.

JISHUMI:v1p689/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p689/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p689/r1.claim: The signs in creation include water apportioned to needs and made into rivers and springs; food for every animal; desire sustaining life; and God’s unique power to give life.
JISHUMI:v1p689/r1.anchor: إخراج الماء بحسب حاجتهم ومصالحهم، فلذلك صيرها أنهارا وينابيع. وخامسها: ما جعل لكل حيوان من الأغذية

JISHUMI:v1p689/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p689/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p689/r2.claim: Further signs are varied forms and organs composed from flowing water, and life’s ordered stages from milk and food to speech, sensation, and reason.
JISHUMI:v1p689/r2.anchor: الصور المختلفة والأعضاء المختلفة والمركبات المتنوعة من اللحم والعظم والعصب والعروق، وجميع ذلك مركب من ماء دافق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.claim: The question from what was he created is answered by he was created from a spurting fluid.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r2.anchor: { مم خلق } استفهام جوابه { خلق من ماء دافق }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r3.claim: Dāfiq may attribute the fluid to the act of pouring, like lābin and tāmir attribute things to their sources.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r3.anchor: النسبة إلى الدفق الذي هو مصدر دفق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r4.claim: Alternatively, dāfiq is a figurative attribution: the pouring properly belongs to the fluid’s owner.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r5.claim: The verse does not say two fluids because they mingle in the womb and unite as human creation begins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736/r5.anchor: لم يقل ماءين لامتزاجهما في الرحم

MUQATIL:86:1-7/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:86:1-7/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:86:1-7/r4.claim: The gushing water is the fluids of the man and woman, which adhere to one another and form the human.
MUQATIL:86:1-7/r4.anchor: خلق من ماء الرجل، والمرأة والتصق بعضه على بعض فخلق منه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r1.claim: Dāfiq describes forceful pouring; strictly the person is the one who pours, so attributing the action to the fluid is figurative.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r1.anchor: والدفق صب فيه دفع والدفق فى الحقيقة لصاحبه والاسناد إلى الماء مجاز

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r2.claim: Some linguists say dafaqt al-māʾ means “I poured the water,” while dafaqa al-māʾ bi-nafsihi means “the water flowed.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r2.anchor: وعن بعض أهل اللغة دفقت الماء دفقا صببته ودفق الماء بنفسه أى انصب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r3.claim: The verse uses singular “water,” not two waters, because the fluids mingle in the womb and unite when human creation begins.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#2/r3.anchor: ولم يقل من ماءين لا متزاجهما فى الرحم واتحادهما حين ابتدئ فى خلقه

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r4.claim: The dāfiq water is semen; dafq means pouring water out, and the word dāfiq describes water poured out.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r4.anchor: { من مآء دافق } أي من المني. والدفق: صب الماء، دفقت الماء أدفقه دفقا: صببته

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r5.claim: Dāfiq is an active-form word with passive sense, like sirr kātim for a secret that is concealed; the expression is based on dufiq al-māʾ, and one does not say dafaqa al-māʾ. Daafa Allah rūḥahu is a curse wishing death.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r5.anchor: فهو ماء دافق، أي مدفوق كما قالوا: سر كاتم: أي مكتوم لأنه من قولك: دفق الماء، على ما لم يسم فاعله

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r6.speaker: الفراء والأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r6.claim: Al-Farra and al-Akhfash gloss dāfiq as water poured into the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r6.anchor: قال الفراء والأخفش: «من ماء دافق» أي مصبوب في الرحم

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes dāfiq as “water possessing an outpouring.”
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r7.anchor: الزجاج: من ماء ذي اندفاق. يقال: دارع وفارس ونابل أي ذو فرس، ودرع، ونبل

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r8.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r8.claim: Sibawayh's analysis makes dāfiq the water flowing with great force.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r8.anchor: وهذا مذهب سيبويه. فالدافق هو المندفق بشدة قوته

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r9.claim: Two fluids, the man's and the woman's, are intended, but are called one water because they mix.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r9.anchor: وأراد ماءين: ماء الرجل وماء المرأة لأن الإنسان مخلوق منهما، لكن جعلهما ماء واحدا لامتزاجهما

QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r10.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r10.claim: Ikrima reports from Ibn Abbas that dāfiq means viscous.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:5-7/r10.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس: «دافق» لزج

QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.claim: Humanity's first creation demonstrates divine determination and governance, showing that people are not abandoned aimlessly or left neglected.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:5/r2.anchor: وتوحي بأن الإنسان ليس متروكا سدى ،  ولا مهملا ضياعا

QUTB-ZILAL:86:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:6/r1.claim: The human was created from a fluid that gushes forth.
